??? quote "Dialogue"

    - *Player*! I have pinned Gorm's scribble over the windlass. The second lift, corrected by the Master of the Stairs himself. Someday!
    - *Player*! New brush, and the rope has never been so well oiled. Up we go?
    - *Player*! Hop in, the basket has missed you. So has the gossip.
    - Hamish, keeper of the lift! Up, down, or something put by in the shed?
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the lift.
        - *Choice:* Anything worrying you?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - Hamish! Keeper of the rope lift these fifteen years. I took it over from old Murdo when his arms gave out. Rode it every day as a boy, whenever he would let me, and some days when he would not.
    - And I raise my nephew Fionn, in the little house by the windlass. Quickest boy on the cliffs. Cheekiest too. Did I tell you what he did last week? I will tell you on the way up.
    - Fionn is my sister Ishbel's boy. His father, Duncan, drowned when he was barely one, and Ishbel went two winters after, with a cough that would not let go.
    - I was thirty-two and had never looked after anything softer than a rope. I took him home to the windlass anyway. Best thing I ever hauled up a cliff. Do not tell him I said so, he will be unbearable.
    - A timber frame bolted into the clifftop, a great windlass, a counterweight of stone-filled baskets in its own channel, and one heavy rope I oil by hand every week. Built long before I was born.
    - It hauls goods and tired legs from the Inlet Quay to the top. And whatever you cannot carry, I keep in my store-shed by the windlass, dry and counted. Fifteen years and I never lost a crate. Never dropped one either.
    - Worrying? Me? Only Fionn, all day long. If he takes a fall while I am at the windlass with a basket halfway up, I cannot let go to run to him.
    - Gorm wrote on my drawing! On it! Moved my anchor bolt a yard over and wrote that the rock would spit it out. He is right, which is worse.
    - And lately, on still nights, the rope gives a shudder. As if something had brushed it, out on the face in the dark. I go out with a lamp and there is nothing. I do not like it.
    - Mind your fingers on the frame!
